#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <numeric>
#include <cmath>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <limits>
#include <chrono>
#include <algorithm>
#include <iomanip>
#include <cstring>
#include <omp.h>


// Thread block size
#define TBSIZE 256

// Number of thread blocks for the DOT kernel 
#define DOT_NUM_BLOCKS 256

// scalar constanst for the mul, triad and nstream kernels
#define SCALAR (0.4)

// Default size of 2^25
int ARRAY_SIZE = 33554432;
unsigned int num_times = 100;


template <class T>
void init_arrays(
  T *__restrict a,
  T *__restrict b,
  T *__restrict c,
  T initA, T initB, T initC)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    a[i] = initA;
    b[i] = initB;
    c[i] = initC;
  }
}


template <class T>
void copy(const T *__restrict a, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
    c[i] = a[i];
}

template <class T>
void mul(T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    b[i] = scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
void add(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void triad(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] = b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void nstream(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] += b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
T dot(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  T sum = 0.0;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd map(tofrom: sum) thread_limit(TBSIZE) reduction(+:sum)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
  {
    sum += a[i] * b[i];
  }
  return sum;
}


// Runs the kernel(s) and prints output.
template <typename T>
void run()
{
  std::streamsize ss = std::cout.precision();

  std::cout << "Running kernels " << num_times << " times" << std::endl;

  // The array size must be divisible by TBSIZE for kernel launches
  if (ARRAY_SIZE % TBSIZE != 0)
  {
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << "Array size must be a multiple of " << TBSIZE;
    throw std::runtime_error(ss.str());
  }

  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  T *a = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *b = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *c = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);

  if (sizeof(T) == sizeof(float))
    std::cout << "Precision: float" << std::endl;
  else
    std::cout << "Precision: double" << std::endl;

  // MB = 10^6
  std::cout << std::setprecision(1) << std::fixed
    << "Array size: " << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout << "Total size: " << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout.precision(ss);

  #pragma omp target data map(alloc: a[0:array_size], b[0:array_size], c[0:array_size])
  {
    // Initialize device arrays
    init_arrays(a, b, c, (T)0.1, (T)0.2, T(0.0));

    // List of times
    std::vector<std::vector<double>> timings(6);

    // Declare timers
    std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::time_point t1, t2;

    // Main loop
    for (unsigned int k = 0; k < num_times; k++)
    {
      // Execute Copy
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      copy(a, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[0].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());


      // Execute Mul
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      mul(b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[1].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Add
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      add(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[2].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Triad
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      triad(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[3].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Dot
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      dot(a, b);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[4].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute NStream
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      nstream(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[5].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());
    }

    // Display timing results
    std::cout
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Function"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "MBytes/sec"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Min (sec)"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Max"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Average"
      << std::endl
      << std::fixed;

    std::vector<std::string> labels;
    std::vector<size_t> sizes;

    labels = {"Copy", "Mul", "Add", "Triad", "Dot", "Nstream"};
    sizes = {
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      4 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE};

    for (size_t i = 0; i < timings.size(); ++i)
    {
      // Get min/max; ignore the first result
      auto minmax = std::minmax_element(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end());

      // Calculate average; ignore the first result
      double average = std::accumulate(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end(), 0.0) / (double)(num_times - 1);

      double bandwidth = 1.0E-6 * sizes[i] / (*minmax.first);

      std::cout
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << labels[i]
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(3) << bandwidth
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.first
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.second
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << average
        << std::endl;
    }
    // Add a blank line
    std::cout << std::endl;

  }

  free(a);
  free(b);
  free(c);
}


int parseUInt(const char *str, unsigned int *output)
{
  char *next;
  *output = strtoul(str, &next, 10);
  return !strlen(next);
}

int parseInt(const char *str, int *output)
{
  char *next;
  *output = strtol(str, &next, 10);
  return !strlen(next);
}

void parseArguments(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++)
  {
    if (!std::string("--arraysize").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-s").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseInt(argv[i], &ARRAY_SIZE) || ARRAY_SIZE <= 0)
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid array size." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--numtimes").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-n").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseUInt(argv[i], &num_times))
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid number of times." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
      if (num_times < 2)
      {
        std::cerr << "Number of times must be 2 or more" << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--help").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-h").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      std::cout << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " [OPTIONS]" << std::endl << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Options:" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -h  --help               Print the message" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -s  --arraysize  SIZE    Use SIZE elements in the array" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -n  --numtimes   NUM     Run the test NUM times (NUM >= 2)" << std::endl;
      std::cout << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }
    else
    {
      std::cerr << "Unrecognized argument '" << argv[i] << "' (try '--help')"
        << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
  }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  parseArguments(argc, argv);
  run<float>();
  run<double>();
}

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.

Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

// Thread block size
#define TBSIZE 256

#define DOT_NUM_BLOCKS 256

// scalar constanst for the mul, triad and nstream kernels
#define SCALAR (0.4)

unsigned int num_times = 100;


template <class T>
void init_arrays(
  T *__restrict a,
  T *__restrict b,
  T *__restrict c,
  T initA, T initB, T initC)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    a[i] = initA;
    b[i] = initB;
    c[i] = initC;
  }
}


template <class T>
void copy(const T *__restrict a, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
    c[i] = a[i];
}

template <class T>
void mul(T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    b[i] = scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
void add(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void triad(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] = b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void nstream(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] += b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
T dot(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  T sum = 0.0;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd map(tofrom: sum) thread_limit(TBSIZE) reduction(+:sum)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
  {
    sum += a[i] * b[i];
  }
  return sum;
}

template <typename T>
void run()
{
  std::streamsize ss = std::cout.precision();

  std::cout << "Running kernels " << num_times << " times" << std::endl;

  // The array size must be divisible by TBSIZE for kernel launches
  if (ARRAY_SIZE % TBSIZE != 0)
  {
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << "Array size must be a multiple of " << TBSIZE;
    throw std::runtime_error(ss.str());
  }

  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  T *a = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *b = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *c = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);

  if (sizeof(T) == sizeof(float))
    std::cout << "Precision: float" << std::endl;
  else
    std::cout << "Precision: double" << std::endl;

  // MB = 10^6
  std::cout << std::setprecision(1) << std::fixed
    << "Array size: " << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout << "Total size: " << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout.precision(ss);

  #pragma omp target data map(alloc: a[0:array_size], b[0:array_size], c[0:array_size])
  {
    // Initialize device arrays
    init_arrays(a, b, c, (T)0.1, (T)0.2, T(0.0));

    // List of times
    std::vector<std::vector<double>> timings(6);

    // Declare timers
    std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::time_point t1, t2;

    // Main loop
    for (unsigned int k = 0; k < num_times; k++)
    {
      // Execute Copy
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      copy(a, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[0].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());


      // Execute Mul
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      mul(b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[1].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Add
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      add(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[2].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Triad

      triad(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[3].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Dot

      dot(a, b);

      timings[4].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      nstream(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[5].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());
    }

    // Display timing results
    std::cout
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Function"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "MBytes/sec"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Min (sec)"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Max"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Average"
      << std::endl
      << std::fixed;

    std::vector<std::string> labels;
    std::vector<size_t> sizes;

    labels = {"Copy", "Mul", "Add", "Triad", "Dot", "Nstream"};
    sizes = {
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      4 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE};

      auto minmax = std::minmax_element(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end());

      // Calculate average; ignore the first result
      double average = std::accumulate(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end(), 0.0) / (double)(num_times - 1);

      double bandwidth = 1.0E-6 * sizes[i] / (*minmax.first);

        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(3) << bandwidth
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.first
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.second
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << average
        << std::endl;
    }
    // Add a blank line
    std::cout << std::endl;

  }

  free(a);
  free(b);
  free(c);
}

{

  {

int main(int argc, char *argv[])

// Thread block size
#define TBSIZE 256

// Number of thread blocks for the DOT kernel 
#define DOT_NUM_BLOCKS 256

// scalar constanst for the mul, triad and nstream kernels
#define SCALAR (0.4)

// Default size of 2^25
int ARRAY_SIZE = 33554432;
unsigned int num_times = 100;


template <class T>
void init_arrays(
  T *__restrict a,
  T *__restrict b,
  T *__restrict c,
  T initA, T initB, T initC)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    a[i] = initA;
    b[i] = initB;
    c[i] = initC;
  }
}


template <class T>
void copy(const T *__restrict a, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
    c[i] = a[i];
}

template <class T>
void mul(T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    b[i] = scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
void add(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void triad(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] = b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void nstream(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] += b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
T dot(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  T sum = 0.0;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd map(tofrom: sum) thread_limit(TBSIZE) reduction(+:sum)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
  {
    sum += a[i] * b[i];
  }
  return sum;
}


// Runs the kernel(s) and prints output.
template <typename T>
void run()
{
  std::streamsize ss = std::cout.precision();

  std::cout << "Running kernels " << num_times << " times" << std::endl;

  // The array size must be divisible by TBSIZE for kernel launches
  if (ARRAY_SIZE % TBSIZE != 0)
  {
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << "Array size must be a multiple of " << TBSIZE;
    throw std::runtime_error(ss.str());
  }

  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  T *a = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *b = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *c = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);

  if (sizeof(T) == sizeof(float))
    std::cout << "Precision: float" << std::endl;
  else
    std::cout << "Precision: double" << std::endl;

  // MB = 10^6
  std::cout << std::setprecision(1) << std::fixed
    << "Array size: " << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout << "Total size: " << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout.precision(ss);

  #pragma omp target data map(alloc: a[0:array_size], b[0:array_size], c[0:array_size])
  {
    // Initialize device arrays
    init_arrays(a, b, c, (T)0.1, (T)0.2, T(0.0));

    // List of times
    std::vector<std::vector<double>> timings(6);

    // Declare timers
    std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::time_point t1, t2;

    // Main loop
    for (unsigned int k = 0; k < num_times; k++)
    {
      // Execute Copy
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      copy(a, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[0].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());


      // Execute Mul
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      mul(b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[1].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Add
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      add(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[2].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Triad
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      triad(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[3].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Dot
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      dot(a, b);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[4].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute NStream
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      nstream(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[5].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());
    }

    // Display timing results
    std::cout
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Function"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "MBytes/sec"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Min (sec)"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Max"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Average"
      << std::endl
      << std::fixed;

    std::vector<std::string> labels;
    std::vector<size_t> sizes;

    labels = {"Copy", "Mul", "Add", "Triad", "Dot", "Nstream"};
    sizes = {
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      4 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE};

    for (size_t i = 0; i < timings.size(); ++i)
    {
      // Get min/max; ignore the first result
      auto minmax = std::minmax_element(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end());

      // Calculate average; ignore the first result
      double average = std::accumulate(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end(), 0.0) / (double)(num_times - 1);

      double bandwidth = 1.0E-6 * sizes[i] / (*minmax.first);

      std::cout
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << labels[i]
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(3) << bandwidth
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.first
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.second
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << average
        << std::endl;
    }
    // Add a blank line
    std::cout << std::endl;

  }

  free(a);
  free(b);
  free(c);
}


int parseUInt(const char *str, unsigned int *output)
{

}

int parseInt(const char *str, int *output)
{

  *output = strtol(str, &next, 10);

}

void parseArguments(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++)
  {
    if (!std::string("--arraysize").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-s").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseInt(argv[i], &ARRAY_SIZE) || ARRAY_SIZE <= 0)
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid array size." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--numtimes").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-n").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseUInt(argv[i], &num_times))
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid number of times." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
      if (num_times < 2)
      {
        std::cerr << "Number of times must be 2 or more" << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--help").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-h").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      std::cout << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " [OPTIONS]" << std::endl << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Options:" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -h  --help               Print the message" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -s  --arraysize  SIZE    Use SIZE elements in the array" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -n  --numtimes   NUM     Run the test NUM times (NUM >= 2)" << std::endl;
      std::cout << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }
    else
    {
      std::cerr << "Unrecognized argument '" << argv[i] << "' (try '--help')"
        << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
  }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  parseArguments(argc, argv);
  run<float>();
  run<double>();
}

## Section 1: Grid Size and Block Size

### General Launch-Configuration Rules

The command-line arguments may not be used directly in the launch site and may instead flow through intermediate variables, helper functions, or derived expressions.

- Ignore code after the first target kernel invocation, because only the first execution matters. If the kernel is launched inside a loop, only analyze the first loop iteration that invokes that kernel.
- If the target kernel is templated, only report the first instantiation that is actually executed.

### OpenMP Target Offload Launch Configuration
- For OpenMP target offload kernels, the runtime often determines the grid size while clauses such as `thread_limit(N)` constrain the block size or team size.
- Do not assume the grid size is simply `ceil(total_iterations / thread_limit)`. OpenMP runtimes commonly distribute work through grid-stride style execution, chunking, or implementation-defined scheduling decisions.

## Section 2: FLOP Counting

### Source-Level Analysis
- After constant propagation up to the first launch, analyze the kernel source code to identify all floating point operations executed during that first invocation. Account for the number of launched threads, loop iterations, and warp divergence regions when scaling the total FLOP counts.
- Preprocessor macros from <compile_commands> may affect control flow and floating point work, so include their impact in your analysis.
- Code comments may incorrectly state the number of FLOPs, so do not trust them; calculate the counts yourself.
- Unary negation of a float or double (for example -x) DOES count as a floating point operation.
- Other floating point datatypes such as FP8 should not be counted as FP16, FP32, or FP64 FLOPs.

### Counting Compiler-Generated FP16 and FP32 Instructions
- Count compiler-generated arithmetic instructions if they execute, even when they originate from helper routines, lowered math-library calls, constant materialization, or implementation details rather than explicit source-level arithmetic.
- The compiler may insert packed FP16 instructions such as HFMA2 / HFMA2_32I for constant or zero materialization on some GPU architectures instead of using MOV-family instructions. If these execute, count them as real FP16 arithmetic in the final estimate: each HFMA2 contributes 4 FP16 FLOPs, but this behavior is architecture- and ptxas-dependent, so infer it conservatively when SASS is unavailable.
- Packed FP16 fused multiply-add instructions contribute multiple FP16 FLOPs per instruction. Lower-precision helper instructions used to implement higher-precision or transcendental operations still count toward the precision at which they execute.
- When SASS is available, count the arithmetic instructions on the taken execution path and scale by how many times that path executes. When SASS is not available, acknowledge that source-only counting may under-estimate lowered helper work and provide the best defensible estimate from the source.
- Compilers may also eliminate common subexpressions or reuse previously computed values, which can reduce the true FLOP count. Use the source and SASS together to avoid over-counting optimized-away work.

### Counting FLOPs from Transcendental and Math Library Functions

- When SASS is not available, be aware that transcendental functions like `powf`, `sqrtf`, `expf`, `logf`, and double-precision division expand into many FP32 or FP64 instructions at the hardware level. Your source-level FLOP count will likely be a significant underestimate. Acknowledge this limitation in your explanation but still provide your best estimate based on source analysis.

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.
- Count only memory traffic attributable to that invocation, not later kernel launches, host-device transfers, or deferred effects outside the invocation being analyzed.
- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them, so reason carefully from the executed source path when estimating actual global-memory traffic.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.
- In many cases, if all the writes fit in the L2 cache, then dram_bytes_written_count will be zero, even if the source code shows many store instructions. Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

#include <omp.h>


// Thread block size
#define TBSIZE 256

// Number of thread blocks for the DOT kernel 
#define DOT_NUM_BLOCKS 256

// scalar constanst for the mul, triad and nstream kernels
#define SCALAR (0.4)

// Default size of 2^25
int ARRAY_SIZE = 33554432;
unsigned int num_times = 100;


template <class T>
void init_arrays(
  T *__restrict a,
  T *__restrict b,
  T *__restrict c,
  T initA, T initB, T initC)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    a[i] = initA;
    b[i] = initB;
    c[i] = initC;
  }
}


template <class T>
void copy(const T *__restrict a, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
    c[i] = a[i];
}

template <class T>
void mul(T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    b[i] = scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
void add(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void triad(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] = b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void nstream(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] += b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
T dot(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  T sum = 0.0;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd map(tofrom: sum) thread_limit(TBSIZE) reduction(+:sum)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
  {
    sum += a[i] * b[i];
  }
  return sum;
}


// Runs the kernel(s) and prints output.
template <typename T>
void run()
{
  std::streamsize ss = std::cout.precision();

  std::cout << "Running kernels " << num_times << " times" << std::endl;

  // The array size must be divisible by TBSIZE for kernel launches
  if (ARRAY_SIZE % TBSIZE != 0)
  {
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << "Array size must be a multiple of " << TBSIZE;
    throw std::runtime_error(ss.str());
  }

  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  T *a = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *b = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *c = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);

  if (sizeof(T) == sizeof(float))
    std::cout << "Precision: float" << std::endl;
  else
    std::cout << "Precision: double" << std::endl;

  // MB = 10^6
  std::cout << std::setprecision(1) << std::fixed
    << "Array size: " << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout << "Total size: " << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout.precision(ss);

  #pragma omp target data map(alloc: a[0:array_size], b[0:array_size], c[0:array_size])
  {
    // Initialize device arrays
    init_arrays(a, b, c, (T)0.1, (T)0.2, T(0.0));

    // List of times
    std::vector<std::vector<double>> timings(6);

    // Declare timers
    std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::time_point t1, t2;

    // Main loop
    for (unsigned int k = 0; k < num_times; k++)
    {
      // Execute Copy
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      copy(a, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[0].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());


      // Execute Mul
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      mul(b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[1].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Add
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      add(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[2].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Triad
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      triad(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[3].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Dot
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      dot(a, b);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[4].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute NStream
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      nstream(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[5].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());
    }

    // Display timing results
    std::cout
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Function"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "MBytes/sec"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Min (sec)"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Max"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Average"
      << std::endl
      << std::fixed;

    std::vector<std::string> labels;
    std::vector<size_t> sizes;

    labels = {"Copy", "Mul", "Add", "Triad", "Dot", "Nstream"};
    sizes = {
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      4 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE};

    for (size_t i = 0; i < timings.size(); ++i)
    {
      // Get min/max; ignore the first result
      auto minmax = std::minmax_element(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end());

      // Calculate average; ignore the first result
      double average = std::accumulate(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end(), 0.0) / (double)(num_times - 1);

      double bandwidth = 1.0E-6 * sizes[i] / (*minmax.first);

      std::cout
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << labels[i]
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(3) << bandwidth
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.first
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.second
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << average
        << std::endl;
    }
    // Add a blank line
    std::cout << std::endl;

  }

  free(a);
  free(b);
  free(c);
}

// Thread block size
#define TBSIZE 256

// Number of thread blocks for the DOT kernel 
#define DOT_NUM_BLOCKS 256

// scalar constanst for the mul, triad and nstream kernels
#define SCALAR (0.4)

// Default size of 2^25
int ARRAY_SIZE = 33554432;
unsigned int num_times = 100;


template <class T>
void init_arrays(
  T *__restrict a,
  T *__restrict b,
  T *__restrict c,
  T initA, T initB, T initC)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    a[i] = initA;
    b[i] = initB;
    c[i] = initC;
  }
}


template <class T>
void copy(const T *__restrict a, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
    c[i] = a[i];
}

template <class T>
void mul(T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    b[i] = scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
void add(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void triad(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] = b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void nstream(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] += b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
T dot(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  T sum = 0.0;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd map(tofrom: sum) thread_limit(TBSIZE) reduction(+:sum)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
  {
    sum += a[i] * b[i];
  }
  return sum;
}

template <typename T>
void run()
{
  std::streamsize ss = std::cout.precision();

  std::cout << "Running kernels " << num_times << " times" << std::endl;

  // The array size must be divisible by TBSIZE for kernel launches
  if (ARRAY_SIZE % TBSIZE != 0)
  {
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << "Array size must be a multiple of " << TBSIZE;
    throw std::runtime_error(ss.str());
  }

  T *b = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *c = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);

  if (sizeof(T) == sizeof(float))
    std::cout << "Precision: float" << std::endl;
  else
    std::cout << "Precision: double" << std::endl;

  std::cout << std::setprecision(1) << std::fixed
    << "Array size: " << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"

  {

    init_arrays(a, b, c, (T)0.1, (T)0.2, T(0.0));

    std::vector<std::vector<double>> timings(6);

    // Declare timers
    std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::time_point t1, t2;

    // Main loop
    for (unsigned int k = 0; k < num_times; k++)
    {
      // Execute Copy
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      copy(a, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[0].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());


      // Execute Mul
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      mul(b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[1].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Add
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      add(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[2].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Triad
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      triad(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[3].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Dot
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      dot(a, b);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[4].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute NStream
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      nstream(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[5].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());
    }

    // Display timing results
    std::cout
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Function"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "MBytes/sec"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Min (sec)"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Max"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Average"
      << std::endl
      << std::fixed;

    std::vector<std::string> labels;
    std::vector<size_t> sizes;

    labels = {"Copy", "Mul", "Add", "Triad", "Dot", "Nstream"};
    sizes = {
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      4 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE};

    for (size_t i = 0; i < timings.size(); ++i)

      // Calculate average; ignore the first result
      double average = std::accumulate(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end(), 0.0) / (double)(num_times - 1);

      double bandwidth = 1.0E-6 * sizes[i] / (*minmax.first);

      std::cout
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << labels[i]
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(3) << bandwidth
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.first
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.second
        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << average
        << std::endl;
    }
    // Add a blank line
    std::cout << std::endl;

  }

  free(a);
  free(b);
  free(c);
}

- Ignore code after the first target kernel invocation, because only the first execution matters. If the kernel is launched inside a loop, only analyze the first loop iteration that invokes that kernel.
- If the target kernel is templated, only report the first instantiation that is actually executed.

### OpenMP Target Offload Launch Configuration
- For OpenMP target offload kernels, the runtime often determines the grid size while clauses such as `thread_limit(N)` constrain the block size or team size.
- Do not assume the grid size is simply `ceil(total_iterations / thread_limit)`. OpenMP runtimes commonly distribute work through grid-stride style execution, chunking, or implementation-defined scheduling decisions.

## Section 2: FLOP Counting

### Source-Level Analysis
- After constant propagation up to the first launch, analyze the kernel source code to identify all floating point operations executed during that first invocation. Account for the number of launched threads, loop iterations, and warp divergence regions when scaling the total FLOP counts.
- Preprocessor macros from <compile_commands> may affect control flow and floating point work, so include their impact in your analysis.
- Code comments may incorrectly state the number of FLOPs, so do not trust them; calculate the counts yourself.
- Unary negation of a float or double (for example -x) DOES count as a floating point operation.
- Other floating point datatypes such as FP8 should not be counted as FP16, FP32, or FP64 FLOPs.

### Counting Compiler-Generated FP16 and FP32 Instructions
- Count compiler-generated arithmetic instructions if they execute, even when they originate from helper routines, lowered math-library calls, constant materialization, or implementation details rather than explicit source-level arithmetic.
- The compiler may insert packed FP16 instructions such as HFMA2 / HFMA2_32I for constant or zero materialization on some GPU architectures instead of using MOV-family instructions. If these execute, count them as real FP16 arithmetic in the final estimate: each HFMA2 contributes 4 FP16 FLOPs, but this behavior is architecture- and ptxas-dependent, so infer it conservatively when SASS is unavailable.
- Packed FP16 fused multiply-add instructions contribute multiple FP16 FLOPs per instruction. Lower-precision helper instructions used to implement higher-precision or transcendental operations still count toward the precision at which they execute.
- When SASS is available, count the arithmetic instructions on the taken execution path and scale by how many times that path executes. When SASS is not available, acknowledge that source-only counting may under-estimate lowered helper work and provide the best defensible estimate from the source.

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.
- Count only memory traffic attributable to that invocation, not later kernel launches, host-device transfers, or deferred effects outside the invocation being analyzed.
- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them, so reason carefully from the executed source path when estimating actual global-memory traffic.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.
- In many cases, if all the writes fit in the L2 cache, then dram_bytes_written_count will be zero, even if the source code shows many store instructions. Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

### Distinguishing Unique Footprint from Total Traffic
- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.
- For DRAM read estimation: if the unique read footprint (distinct cache lines touched) fits in L2, then after the first compulsory miss, subsequent reads of the same addresses in inner-loop iterations will hit in cache. In this case, DRAM bytes read ≈ unique footprint, not total_loads × element_size.
- For DRAM write estimation: if the unique write footprint fits in L2, then repeated stores to the same addresses will overwrite the same cache lines without eviction, and DRAM bytes written ≈ 0 during the kernel (the dirty lines remain in L2 until a later eviction event).
- Always compute both the unique footprint and the total traffic, then use the L2 cache size to determine which estimate is appropriate.

### Stencil and Streaming Access Patterns
- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.
- When the working set is much larger than L2, account for the possibility of cache-line eviction and refetch rather than assuming perfect reuse.
- When the working set fits in L2, DRAM traffic may be close to the unique footprint loaded once and then reused from cache.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

#include <iostream>

#include <cmath>
#include <cstdlib>
#include <limits>
#include <chrono>
#include <algorithm>
#include <iomanip>
#include <cstring>
#include <omp.h>


// Thread block size
#define TBSIZE 256

// Number of thread blocks for the DOT kernel 
#define DOT_NUM_BLOCKS 256

// scalar constanst for the mul, triad and nstream kernels
#define SCALAR (0.4)

// Default size of 2^25
int ARRAY_SIZE = 33554432;
unsigned int num_times = 100;


template <class T>
void init_arrays(
  T *__restrict a,
  T *__restrict b,
  T *__restrict c,
  T initA, T initB, T initC)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    a[i] = initA;
    b[i] = initB;
    c[i] = initC;
  }
}


template <class T>
void copy(const T *__restrict a, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
    c[i] = a[i];
}

template <class T>
void mul(T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    b[i] = scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
void add(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void triad(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] = b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void nstream(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] += b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
T dot(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  T sum = 0.0;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd map(tofrom: sum) thread_limit(TBSIZE) reduction(+:sum)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
  {
    sum += a[i] * b[i];
  }
  return sum;
}


// Runs the kernel(s) and prints output.
template <typename T>
void run()
{
  std::streamsize ss = std::cout.precision();

  std::cout << "Running kernels " << num_times << " times" << std::endl;

  // The array size must be divisible by TBSIZE for kernel launches
  if (ARRAY_SIZE % TBSIZE != 0)
  {
    std::stringstream ss;
    ss << "Array size must be a multiple of " << TBSIZE;
    throw std::runtime_error(ss.str());
  }

  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  T *a = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *b = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);
  T *c = (T*)aligned_alloc(1024, sizeof(T)*array_size);

  if (sizeof(T) == sizeof(float))
    std::cout << "Precision: float" << std::endl;
  else
    std::cout << "Precision: double" << std::endl;

  // MB = 10^6
  std::cout << std::setprecision(1) << std::fixed
    << "Array size: " << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"
    << " (=" << ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-9 << " GB)" << std::endl;
  std::cout << "Total size: " << 3.0*ARRAY_SIZE*sizeof(T)*1.0E-6 << " MB"

  std::cout.precision(ss);

    init_arrays(a, b, c, (T)0.1, (T)0.2, T(0.0));

    // List of times
    std::vector<std::vector<double>> timings(6);

    // Declare timers
    std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::time_point t1, t2;

    // Main loop
    for (unsigned int k = 0; k < num_times; k++)
    {
      // Execute Copy
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      copy(a, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[0].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());


      // Execute Mul
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      mul(b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[1].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Add
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      add(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[2].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      // Execute Triad
      t1 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      triad(a, b, c);
      t2 = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();
      timings[3].push_back(std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::duration<double> >(t2 - t1).count());

      dot(a, b);

      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "MBytes/sec"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Min (sec)"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Max"
      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Average"
      << std::endl
      << std::fixed;

    std::vector<size_t> sizes;

      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      3 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      2 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE,
      4 * sizeof(T) * ARRAY_SIZE};

    for (size_t i = 0; i < timings.size(); ++i)
    {
      // Get min/max; ignore the first result
      auto minmax = std::minmax_element(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end());

      // Calculate average; ignore the first result
      double average = std::accumulate(timings[i].begin()+1, timings[i].end(), 0.0) / (double)(num_times - 1);

      double bandwidth = 1.0E-6 * sizes[i] / (*minmax.first);

        << std::left << std::setw(12) << labels[i]

        << std::left << std::setw(12) << std::setprecision(5) << *minmax.second

        << std::endl;
    }

    std::cout << std::endl;

  free(b);
  free(c);

void parseArguments(int argc, char *argv[])

  {

    {

{

int parseUInt(const char *str, unsigned int *output)
{
  char *next;
  *output = strtoul(str, &next, 10);
  return !strlen(next);
}

int parseInt(const char *str, int *output)
{
  char *next;
  *output = strtol(str, &next, 10);
  return !strlen(next);
}

void parseArguments(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++)
  {
    if (!std::string("--arraysize").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-s").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseInt(argv[i], &ARRAY_SIZE) || ARRAY_SIZE <= 0)
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid array size." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--numtimes").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-n").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseUInt(argv[i], &num_times))
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid number of times." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
      if (num_times < 2)
      {
        std::cerr << "Number of times must be 2 or more" << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--help").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-h").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      std::cout << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " [OPTIONS]" << std::endl << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Options:" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -h  --help               Print the message" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -s  --arraysize  SIZE    Use SIZE elements in the array" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -n  --numtimes   NUM     Run the test NUM times (NUM >= 2)" << std::endl;
      std::cout << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }
    else
    {
      std::cerr << "Unrecognized argument '" << argv[i] << "' (try '--help')"
        << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
  }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  parseArguments(argc, argv);
  run<float>();
  run<double>();
}

### Source-Level Analysis

- Preprocessor macros from <compile_commands> may affect control flow and floating point work, so include their impact in your analysis.

- Unary negation of a float or double (for example -x) DOES count as a floating point operation.

### SASS-Guided FLOP Counting

## Section 3: DRAM Read and Write Byte Counting

### General Principles
- Estimate DRAM bytes read and DRAM bytes written for the same first invocation of the kernel.
- Count only memory traffic attributable to that invocation, not later kernel launches, host-device transfers, or deferred effects outside the invocation being analyzed.
- Although the source may show many reads and writes, the compiler may optimize, combine, or eliminate some of them. If SASS is provided, use the global load and store instructions in SASS, especially LDG and STG, to identify the actual global-memory traffic generated by execution.

### Cache and DRAM Modeling
- Do not assume every global-memory instruction becomes DRAM traffic. Some LDG operations may be serviced by the L2 cache instead of DRAM, so only count the loads that correspond to DRAM accesses when estimating dram_bytes_read_count.
- For writes, only count the bytes that go beyond the L2 cache and actually reach DRAM when estimating dram_bytes_written_count. Consider the L2 cache size from <gpu_roofline_specs> together with the amount of store traffic to estimate whether written data fits in cache or spills through to DRAM.
- In many cases, if all the writes fit in the L2 cache, then dram_bytes_written_count will be zero, even if the source code shows many store instructions. Recall that the CUDA L2 cache is a write-back cache at the device-scope visibility, so it does not flush to the DRAM until evictions occur. Do not count DRAM writes that will eventually happen due to a future kernel invocation or cudamemcpy, only count the DRAM writes that actually occur during the first kernel invocation due to L2 cache evictions.

- Distinguish the unique data footprint from total load/store traffic. A kernel may execute many memory instructions while repeatedly touching the same cache lines.

- For stencil or neighbor-based kernels, overlapping accesses can make DRAM traffic much closer to the unique input footprint than to the raw count of source-level loads.

### Write Traffic Amplification
- For streaming write patterns where the output footprint is larger than L2, actual DRAM write traffic can exceed the unique write footprint because of cache behavior and write-allocation effects. Use the unique footprint as a baseline and adjust only when the access pattern or hardware evidence justifies it.

// Thread block size
#define TBSIZE 256

// Number of thread blocks for the DOT kernel 
#define DOT_NUM_BLOCKS 256

// scalar constanst for the mul, triad and nstream kernels
#define SCALAR (0.4)

// Default size of 2^25
int ARRAY_SIZE = 33554432;
unsigned int num_times = 100;


template <class T>
void init_arrays(
  T *__restrict a,
  T *__restrict b,
  T *__restrict c,
  T initA, T initB, T initC)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE; 
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    a[i] = initA;
    b[i] = initB;
    c[i] = initC;
  }
}


template <class T>
void copy(const T *__restrict a, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++)
    c[i] = a[i];
}

template <class T>
void mul(T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    b[i] = scalar * c[i];
  }
}

template <class T>
void add(const T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void triad(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)
{
  const int array_size = ARRAY_SIZE;
  #pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)
  for (int i = 0; i < array_size; i++) {
    const T scalar = SCALAR;
    a[i] = b[i] + scalar * c[i];
  }
}


template <class T>
void nstream(T *__restrict a, const T *__restrict b, const T *__restrict c)

      << std::left << std::setw(12) << "Max"

int parseUInt(const char *str, unsigned int *output)
{
  char *next;
  *output = strtoul(str, &next, 10);
  return !strlen(next);
}

int parseInt(const char *str, int *output)
{
  char *next;
  *output = strtol(str, &next, 10);
  return !strlen(next);
}

void parseArguments(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  for (int i = 1; i < argc; i++)
  {
    if (!std::string("--arraysize").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-s").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseInt(argv[i], &ARRAY_SIZE) || ARRAY_SIZE <= 0)
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid array size." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--numtimes").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-n").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      if (++i >= argc || !parseUInt(argv[i], &num_times))
      {
        std::cerr << "Invalid number of times." << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
      if (num_times < 2)
      {
        std::cerr << "Number of times must be 2 or more" << std::endl;
        exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
      }
    }
    else if (!std::string("--help").compare(argv[i]) ||
        !std::string("-h").compare(argv[i]))
    {
      std::cout << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Usage: " << argv[0] << " [OPTIONS]" << std::endl << std::endl;
      std::cout << "Options:" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -h  --help               Print the message" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -s  --arraysize  SIZE    Use SIZE elements in the array" << std::endl;
      std::cout << "  -n  --numtimes   NUM     Run the test NUM times (NUM >= 2)" << std::endl;
      std::cout << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_SUCCESS);
    }
    else
    {
      std::cerr << "Unrecognized argument '" << argv[i] << "' (try '--help')"
        << std::endl;
      exit(EXIT_FAILURE);
    }
  }
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[])
{
  parseArguments(argc, argv);
  run<float>();
  run<double>();
}

prediction.gridSz_explanation: This is an OpenMP target offload kernel implementing a dot product reduction over ARRAY_SIZE=33554432 elements with thread_limit(TBSIZE=256). The SASS shows a complex cooperative kernel with inter-CTA synchronization using atomics (ATOMG.E.INC, ATOMG.E.OR) and CCTL.IVALL instructions, which is characteristic of an OpenMP runtime that launches a persistent grid. The SASS references c[0x0][0xc] which appears to be the number of CTAs, and the code uses 0x400 (1024) as a bound check (at offset 0x1070: ISETP.GE.U32.AND P0, PT, R17, 0x400, PT) and 0x3ff as a mask. This strongly suggests the runtime launches 1024 thread blocks. The kernel uses a grid-stride loop pattern where blocks cooperatively process the entire array.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The thread_limit(TBSIZE) clause with TBSIZE=256 sets the block size. The SASS confirms this with SHF.L.U32 R52, R17, 0x8, RZ (shifting CTAID by 8 = multiplying by 256) to compute the starting index for each block, consistent with 256 threads per block.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: The dot kernel computes sum += a[i] * b[i] for 33554432 elements. Each element requires 1 FMUL + 1 FADD = 2 FP32 ops, but the SASS uses FFMA (fused multiply-add) which counts as 2 FP32 ops per instruction. So the main computation loop contributes 33554432 * 2 = 67108864 FP32 ops from the FFMA instructions. Additionally, there is a warp-level reduction phase. With 256 threads per block, there are 8 warps. Each warp does a tree reduction with 5 FADD steps (log2(32) = 5 shuffle-add steps), giving 8 warps * 5 FADDs = 40 FADDs per block. Then there's a cross-warp reduction: the 8 partial sums are reduced, requiring about 7 more FADDs. Per block: ~47 FADDs for reduction. For 1024 blocks: 1024 * 47 = 48128 FADDs. Then there's the final reduction across blocks done by the last CTA, summing 1024 partial results with ~1023 FADDs. Plus the final FADD at offset 0x1fd0 for the global accumulation. Also, the FADD at 0x0ec0 (R25 + R54) executes once per grid-stride iteration per thread. The grid-stride loop: each block of 256 threads processes chunks. Total iterations of the outer loop per block = ceil(33554432 / (1024*256)) = ceil(128) = 128 iterations. Each iteration has the FADD at 0x0ec0 for 256 threads = 256 FADDs, plus the warp reduction FADDs. So per outer iteration per block: 256 FADDs (from 0x0ec0) + ~47 reduction FADDs = 303. Over 128 iterations: 128 * 303 * 1024 ≈ but wait, the FFMA in the inner loop already accounts for the main work. Let me reconsider: FFMA at 0x05f0 executes once per element = 33554432 times total, contributing 33554432 * 2 = 67108864 FP32 ops. The FADD at 0x0ec0 executes once per outer-loop iteration per thread. With 128 iterations and 256*1024 threads (but only 256 active per block per iteration): 128 * 256 * 1024 = but that's 33554432, one per element... no, 0x0ec0 is outside the inner loop, once per grid-stride chunk. 128 iterations * 1024 blocks = 131072 FADDs from 0x0ec0. Warp reductions: 128 iterations * 1024 blocks * ~47 = ~6,160,384. The last-block final reduction sums 1024 values ≈ 1023 FADDs. Plus FADD at 0x1fd0 = 1. Total FP32 ≈ 67108864 + 131072 + 6160384 + 1024 ≈ 73,401,344. Approximating: ~73,400,000.

prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: The kernel reads two float arrays a[] and b[] of size 33554432 each. Each array is 33554432 * 4 = 134217728 bytes. Total unique read footprint = 2 * 134217728 = 268435456 bytes. The L2 cache is 5 MB = 5242880 bytes, which is far smaller than the 256 MB read footprint, so nearly all reads must come from DRAM. Additionally, there's a small amount of reads for the reduction buffer (1024 * 4 = 4096 bytes for the partial sums read by the last block), but this fits in L2. The DRAM reads are approximately 268435456 bytes. There's also the LDG at 0x0fd0 reading the reduction buffer pointer (8 bytes) and the final LDG at 0x1fc0 reading the output sum (4 bytes), but these are negligible and likely cached.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The kernel writes partial sums to a reduction buffer. Each of the 1024 blocks writes one float (4 bytes) via ST.E at offset 0x10f0, totaling 1024 * 4 = 4096 bytes. The last block then reads these, computes the final sum, and writes the result via STG.E.64 (8 bytes to zero out the buffer) and STG.E (4 bytes for the final result). The total write footprint is about 4096 + 8 + 4 = 4108 bytes, which easily fits in the 5 MB L2 cache. Since the L2 is write-back and the total written data is tiny compared to L2 capacity, no evictions to DRAM are expected during this kernel invocation. Therefore DRAM bytes written ≈ 0.

prediction.gridSz_explanation: From host code, the first invocation of the target kernel is the first `copy<float>(a,c)` inside `for (k=0; k<num_times; k++)`, after `init_arrays`. With no CLI arguments, `ARRAY_SIZE=33554432` and `TBSIZE=256`. The OpenMP directive uses `thread_limit(256)`, and the SASS shows `SHF.L.U32 R7, R4, 0x8` so each CTA covers a base logical index of `blockIdx.x*256`. The kernel also computes `R0 = c[0x0][0xc] << 8`, then repeatedly increments `R7` by `R0`, indicating an OpenMP grid-stride over teams. Thus block size is fixed at 256 threads, while the actual number of CTAs is runtime-chosen. A defensible estimate is the common libomptarget launch of one team per SM for a simple teams distribute loop on A100, i.e. 108 CTAs; SASS confirms the kernel supports grid-stride execution rather than requiring `ceil(N/256)` CTAs.
prediction.blockSz_explanation: `#pragma omp target teams distribute parallel for simd thread_limit(TBSIZE)` with `TBSIZE=256` constrains the CUDA block/team size. The SASS uses `SR_TID.X` and shifts CTAID by 8 bits (`<< 8`), directly consistent with 256 threads per block.

In the SASS there is one `HFMA2.MMA` used for constant materialization/control setup, but that is FP16 arithmetic, not FP32, and there are no executed FP32 arithmetic instructions on the steady-state copy path.

prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: Although the source has no arithmetic, the SASS contains one executed `HFMA2.MMA R17, -RZ, RZ, 0, 5.9604644775390625e-08` in the active path before the per-thread copy loop. `HFMA2` is a packed half-precision FMA, contributing 4 FP16 FLOPs per executing thread. It executes once for each participating thread that enters the copy region; with the estimated launch of 108 blocks × 256 threads = 27648 threads, that yields 27648×4 = 110592 FP16 FLOPs.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each copied float element requires one 4-byte load from `a`, so the unique input footprint of the first invocation is `33554432 * 4 = 134217728` bytes. The access is a single streaming pass over a 128 MiB array, much larger than the 40 MiB L2, so essentially the whole input footprint must be fetched from DRAM once; repeated accesses are absent despite the grid-stride implementation.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each copied float element produces one 4-byte store to `c`, so the unique output footprint is also 134217728 bytes. Because the kernel writes a 128 MiB array, far exceeding the 40 MiB L2 capacity, dirty lines cannot all remain resident; a streaming store of this size will evict and write back essentially the whole output footprint during the invocation, so DRAM writes are approximated by the unique stored bytes.

prediction.gridSz_explanation: This is an OpenMP target offload kernel with `thread_limit(256)` and ARRAY_SIZE=33554432. The SASS shows a grid-stride loop pattern where R0 = gridDim.x * 256 is the stride. The OpenMP runtime on clang for A100 typically launches enough teams to cover the iteration space. With 33554432 elements and 256 threads per block, ceil(33554432/256) = 131072 blocks. However, OpenMP runtimes often cap the number of teams. Looking at the SASS, the kernel uses a grid-stride loop, meaning fewer CTAs can handle the full iteration space. A common heuristic for clang's OpenMP runtime on A100 is to launch num_SMs * some_factor teams, but with this simple kernel the runtime typically launches exactly ceil(array_size/TBSIZE) = 131072 teams since the iteration space divides evenly. Given the grid-stride loop structure visible in SASS, the runtime may launch fewer. For clang OpenMP targeting sm_80, a typical launch is 131072 teams (one per chunk of 256 elements).
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The `thread_limit(TBSIZE)` clause with TBSIZE=256 sets the block size to 256 threads. The SASS confirms this with `SHF.L.U32 R9, R4, 0x8, RZ` (shift left by 8 = multiply CTAID by 256) and the use of SR_TID.X for thread indexing within a block of 256.
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: The kernel performs `b[i] = scalar * c[i]` for each of the 33554432 elements. That's one FMUL per element = 33554432 FP32 FLOPs. The SASS confirms a single `FMUL R19, R12, 0.40000000596046447754` instruction in the inner loop, executed once per element.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: No double-precision operations are present in this kernel. The template is instantiated with float, and the SASS shows only FP32 instructions (FMUL). No FP64 instructions are visible.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: The SASS shows one HFMA2.MMA instruction at address 0x0260: `HFMA2.MMA R17, -RZ, RZ, 0, 5.9604644775390625e-08`. This is used for constant materialization (creating the value 2^-24 which likely represents the stride increment value 1 in integer context, or is used as a helper). This instruction executes once per CTA entry into the inner work section. With 131072 CTAs and 256 threads per CTA, but this instruction is inside a conditional block that only some threads reach. Looking more carefully, the HFMA2 is inside the P2-taken branch (before the inner loop), executed once per thread that has work. With 33554432 elements and each thread processing exactly 1 element (since grid covers the full space), each thread enters the loop body once. The HFMA2 executes once per thread that enters the loop = 33554432 times. Each HFMA2 counts as 4 FP16 FLOPs (2 FMAs on packed FP16).
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: The kernel reads array c[] (33554432 floats = 128 MB) via LDG.E instructions. The total unique read footprint is 33554432 * 4 = 134217728 bytes. This is 128 MB, which far exceeds the 40 MB L2 cache, so essentially all reads go to DRAM.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The kernel writes array b[] (33554432 floats = 128 MB) via STG.E instructions. The total unique write footprint is 33554432 * 4 = 134217728 bytes. This is 128 MB, which far exceeds the 40 MB L2 cache, so the writes will spill through to DRAM. Since this is a streaming write pattern with no prior read of the same locations, write-allocate policy may cause additional read-for-ownership traffic, but we count only the write bytes here: 134217728 bytes.

The SASS shows a grid-stride loop pattern where each block processes 256 elements per iteration and strides by gridDim.x * 256. For the A100 with 108 SMs, the clang OpenMP runtime typically launches a number of teams equal to ceil(ARRAY_SIZE / TBSIZE) = 33554432/256 = 131072, but examining the SASS more carefully: the grid-stride loop at .L_x_152 with R8 = c[0x0][0xc] (gridDim.x) shifted left by 8 (multiplied by 256) suggests the runtime may choose a smaller grid. However, for clang's OpenMP offload targeting NVIDIA GPUs, the typical behavior is to launch ceil(N/block_size) teams. With ARRAY_SIZE=33554432 and TBSIZE=256, that gives 131072 blocks. This is the most defensible estimate.

The second at 0x0270 executes once per inner loop entry. The first HFMA2 executes for all threads that pass the initial exit check (all 33554432 threads). So total FP16 FLOPs = 33554432 * 4 + 33554432 * 4 = 268435456.

metrics_explanations.fp64_flop_explanation: The double‑precision version is not the first invocation; for the float copy kernel there are no FP64 operations.
metrics_explanations.fp16_flop_explanation: The copy kernel performs only a memory copy (c[i] = a[i]) with no floating‑point arithmetic, so zero FP16 operations.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_read_explanation: Each of the 33,554,432 float elements (4 B) is read once from global memory. The total unique read footprint (128 MiB) exceeds the 40 MiB L2 cache, so essentially all reads miss L2 and go to DRAM.
metrics_explanations.dram_bytes_written_explanation: Each element is written once (4 B). The write footprint also exceeds L2, causing write‑back to DRAM during the kernel, so DRAM bytes written ≈ total bytes written (128 MiB).

prediction.gridSz_explanation: The kernel is `copy<float>` with ARRAY_SIZE = 33554432 and thread_limit(TBSIZE=256). The OpenMP runtime for clang targeting NVIDIA GPUs typically launches ceil(ARRAY_SIZE / TBSIZE) = 33554432 / 256 = 131072 teams. So gridSz = [131072, 1, 1].
prediction.blockSz_explanation: The `thread_limit(TBSIZE)` clause with TBSIZE=256 sets the block size to 256 threads. So blockSz = [256, 1, 1].
prediction.fp32_flop_explanation: The copy kernel simply does `c[i] = a[i]` for float elements. There are no floating point arithmetic operations — just loads and stores of float values. Therefore FP32 FLOP count is 0.
prediction.fp64_flop_explanation: There are no double-precision operations in the copy<float> kernel. FP64 FLOP count is 0.
prediction.fp16_flop_explanation: There are no half-precision operations in the copy kernel. FP16 FLOP count is 0.
prediction.dram_bytes_read_explanation: The kernel reads 33554432 float elements from array `a`, which is 33554432 * 4 = 134217728 bytes. The total read footprint is 128 MB, which far exceeds the 5 MB L2 cache, so essentially all reads go to DRAM. DRAM bytes read ≈ 134217728 bytes.
prediction.dram_bytes_written_explanation: The kernel writes 33554432 float elements to array `c`, which is 33554432 * 4 = 134217728 bytes. The total write footprint is 128 MB, far exceeding the 5 MB L2 cache, so writes will evict through to DRAM. DRAM bytes written ≈ 134217728 bytes.
